name: Caro-Kann Defence
summary: The Caro-Kann (1.e4 c6 followed by ...d5) is one of Black's most solid answers to 1.e4. Black challenges the centre with ...d5 but keeps the c8-bishop free to develop to f5 or g4 before playing ...e6, so Black gets a French-style pawn structure without the French's bad bishop. The price is a little less space and slower counterplay, but Black's position has very few weaknesses, the endgames are usually pleasant, and White's aggressive tries (Advance, Martian and Alien gambits) can be met with clear, principled plans.
keyIdeas: Get the light-squared bishop out (...Bf5 or ...Bg4) BEFORE playing ...e6.
Against the Advance (3.e5), attack the base of White's chain with ...c5 (sometimes ...f6), supported by ...Nc6/...Nd7, ...Ne7 and ...Qb6.
In the Classical (4...Bf5), cover e5 with ...Nd7 before ...Ngf6 and meet h4 with ...h6 so the bishop can retreat to h7.
Trade pieces when you have less space; the c6/e6 structure is excellent in endgames.
Against the Alien (5.Ng5 vs 4...Nf6) play 5...e6!; against the Martian (5.Ng5 vs 4...Bf5) play 6...Nd7, or 6...h6 only if you know 7.Ne6 fxe6 8.Ne5 Bf5!.
If a gambit is accepted, strike back in the centre (...c5) and give material back only to kill the attack.
In the Exchange/Panov, recapture with the c-pawn, develop the bishop to g4 or blockade d5, and target the isolated d-pawn.
typicalPlans: Advance: ...Bf5, ...e6, ...c5, ...Nc6/...Nd7, ...Ne7-f5 or ...Ne7-c6, ...Qb6 pressure on d4 and b2.
Classical: ...Bf5-g6, ...h6, ...Nd7, ...e6, ...Ngf6, ...Be7 or ...Bd6, castle, then ...Qd5/...Qc7 and the ...c5 break.
Panov IQP: blockade d5 with a knight, trade minor pieces, then attack the isolated pawn with ...Rd8 and ...Nf5/...Nb4.
Against gambits: accept when it is sound to do so, return the king to safety (...e6, ...Kg8), develop with tempo and trade White's attackers.
commonMistakes: Playing ...e6 before ...Bf5 in the Advance, locking the bishop in.

lines.name: Classical: Main line 6.h4 h6 7.Nf3 Nd7 8.h5
lines.description: The most important Caro-Kann main line (B19). Black develops the c8-bishop first, swaps it off on d3, then builds the rock-solid ...e6/...c6 structure, castles and frees the game with ...Qd5 or ...c5. Sidelines at move 5: 5.Nc5 b6 6.Nb3 e6 7.Nf3 Nf6 (bishop stays on f5, plan ...Bd6, ...O-O, ...c5); 5.Qf3 e6 6.Ne2 Nd7 (or 6...Bxe4 7.Qxe4 Nf6); 5.Nc3 e6 6.Nf3 Nf6 7.Bd3 Bxd3 8.Qxd3 Nbd7 with easy equality. 5.Ng5 is the Martian Gambit (see those lines). Rare 2nd moves: 2.c3 d5 3.e5 Bf5 4.d4 e6 transposes to the Advance (see advance-c3). Other 6th moves: 6.Bf4 e6 (or 6...Nf6) 7.Nf3 Nf6 and ...Nbd7; 6.Bc4 e6 7.Qe2 (or 7.N1e2) Nf6 with ...Nbd7 and ...Bd6. If White avoids 4.Nxe4 with 4.Nge2?!, play 4...Nf6 5.Ng3 Bg4 with a good game. 6.Be3 e6 (or 6...Nf6) 7.h4 h6 leads to similar play.
lines.evaluation: Roughly equal; White has a little space (+0.3)

lines.name: Advance: Short Variation 4.Nf3 e6 5.Be2 c5 6.Be3
lines.description: The modern main line of the Advance (B12). Black hits d4 with ...c5, develops ...Nd7/...Ne7 and lets White open the position with c4, then gets active pieces on d5. Against 6.O-O or 6.c3 play 6...Nc6 7.c3 cxd4 8.cxd4 Nge7 9.Nc3 Bg4!, swapping the f3-knight and putting a knight on f5 to attack d4. 5...Nd7 (or 5...Ne7) with ...h6 and ...c5 later is a calmer alternative. 6...Qb6!? 7.O-O Qxb2 is the sharp engine choice but needs memorisation. After 4.Nf3 e6: 5.c3 c5 6.Be2 Nc6 (see 6.O-O line); 5.Nbd2 c5 6.Bb5+ Nd7; 5.a4 c5. 5.Bd3 Bxd3 6.Qxd3 c5 is also comfortable for Black. 5.Be3 is met by 5...Qb6 6.Qc1 c5 (or 5...Nd7), the same idea as in the 4.Be3 line.

lines.description: 3.Nd2 is played almost as often as 3.Nc3.
